archetypes.name: routing-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan enumerates specific SKILL.md line numbers (~1059, ~1303, ~1334, ~1336, ~1338, ~1340, Gate-B-bypass, run-step3-review.sh) that must be retargeted to route through the Step 3b completion boundary before Step 4; missing any one path means Step 4 can run without FINALIZE, silently breaking artifact guarantees.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/SKILL.md` and enumerate every prose location — blockquotes, routing diagrams, Gate-B-bypass paragraphs, cap-reached/tally-error/panel-failed paths, and any `run-step3-review.sh` routing annotations — that currently names Step 4 as the next step after Step 3b using any routing verb (continue, proceed, auto-continue, route, jump, enter, go) or arrow/comma shorthand (Step 3b → Step 4, Step 3b/4, Step 3b, then Step 4). Cross-check that list against every location the plan claims to retarget. Flag any path the plan does not mention that would allow Step 4 to be entered without passing through the Step 3b completion boundary fence. Also verify the anti-halt blockquote wording preserves the exact substring `Continue to Step 4 IMMEDIATELY` while still naming the boundary fence as a required prior step. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan prescribes specific new assertions in test-design-structure.sh (region-scoped FINALIZE placement, entry-fence-scoped SIMPLE checks, routing guards, exit-code pins, pause/resume fixture) that must exactly mirror the new SKILL.md structure; a mismatch between the planned harness assertions and the planned SKILL.md edits would let structural regressions pass CI silently.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `scripts/test-design-structure.sh` and `scripts/test-design-structure.md` alongside the plan's harness section. For each new assertion the plan specifies — region-scoped FINALIZE placement between step:3b and step:4, entry-fence-scoped SIMPLE sentinel assertions, negative check for NO_SKETCHES_CLASSIFIED_SIMPLE in the SIMPLE branch subsection, routing guard pattern, exit-code pins for both FINALIZE failure branches, and the pause/resume compatibility fixture — verify that the assertion methodology described (awk slices, between-marker patterns, line-scoped grep) is precise enough to distinguish the new layout from the old without false-positive passes or false-negative failures. Check whether `assert_bash_fences_have_pause_check` will fire for the new Step 3b completion fence and the modified Step 4 entry fence given the canonical two-line prelude requirement. Flag any harness assertion the plan calls for that is underspecified or that conflicts with existing positive pins at lines 344, 371-379, 1568. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cross-doc-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan requires caller-annotation updates in three reference docs (sketch-launch.md, design-driver.md, finalize-plan.md); if any doc still names the old call site or omits the compatibility-guard caveat, consumers of those docs will have an incorrect mental model of where FINALIZE and SIMPLE sentinels originate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/references/sketch-launch.md`, `skills/design/scripts/design-driver.md`, and `skills/design/scripts/finalize-plan.md`. For each, identify every sentence that names a primary caller, call site, or sequencing contract for FINALIZE or SIMPLE sentinel writes. Cross-check against what the plan specifies: design-driver.md and finalize-plan.md must name the Step 3b completion boundary as the primary caller with a compatibility-guard note for Step 4; sketch-launch.md must replace its standalone SIMPLE bash block with prose that attributes sentinel writes solely to the Step 2a entry fence. Flag any normative claim in these docs that would remain correct after only the plan's specified edits, versus any claim that the plan appears to omit updating, or that could be read as implying a second write site. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
